content: # graph-manager: remove terminal statuses (working / idle / other) from the UI (GMD-15) ## What to build The user doesn't want terminal statuses in graph-manager's UI at all. Remove every place where a terminal is shown as `working`, `idle` or `other`/`exited`, along with every UI built on those states: filter chips, NEEDS YOU, badges, amber "waiting on you", nav rows and badge, the Runs "Terminals idle" card, `Ctrl Space a`, and the palette's terminal status. A terminal is shown by its title, workspace and foreground process (`TerminalInfo.process`). Keep these: - **The exited bar inside a terminal pane:** "Process exited with code N" with **Restart** and **Close**. It is the only way to restart a terminal. - **The reconnecting bar.** - **Run chips and pane numbers.** - **All run statuses.** - **The server.** Don't change it: `GET /api/terminals` still returns `status`, `exitCode`, `lastOutputAt` and `process`. The UI reads `status === "exited"` / `exitCode` only to decide whether to show the pane's exited bar. The spec is `docs/prd/graph-manager-no-terminal-status.md`. **Never modify anything under `packages/graph-execution/`.** This is a client-only change, in `apps/graph-manager/src/web/` plus docs. ## Context: files to read before implementing All paths are under `apps/graph-manager/src/web/` unless noted. - `Shell.tsx`: - lines ~15–25: the counts object with `working` and `idle` - line ~134: `termDot` - lines ~151–155: the status block, with 4 `StatusRow`s - lines ~174–188: the Terminals `NavItem` badge, showing `working · idle` in colour - `pages/Runs.tsx`: - line ~282: `const idle = terminals.filter(…"idle")` - lines ~405–416: the "Terminals idle" card `` - the `.runs-cards` grid in `pages/Runs.css`, which has 4 columns - `pages/TerminalSidebar.tsx`: - lines 9–20: `TermFilter`, `FILTERS`, `matchesFilter` - lines 37–64: `workingFor`, `idleFor` and `subLine`, which renders `bash · working 14s`, `… · idle 4m`, `exited 0 · 22m ago` - lines 74–92: `groupTerminals`, which builds the NEEDS YOU section from idle terminals - lines ~118–160: the counts and the three filter chips - line ~170: `subTone`, and the status glyph on each item - line ~220: "No terminals match this filter." - line ~224: the footer hint `Ctrl Space a next idle` - line ~235: `shownOrder(terminals, workspaces, filter)` - `pages/TerminalPane.tsx`: - line 13: imports `idleFor` - lines ~104–118: the header status badge (`working` / `idle … · waiting on you` / `exited N`) and the `.idle` class on the pane - lines ~140–150: the exited bar. **Keep it.** - `pages/Terminals.tsx`: - line ~72: `parseFilter(params.get("filter"))` - lines ~186–200: close, where a `working` terminal asks first - lines ~240–255: `onFilter`, and `order = shownOrder(…, filter)` - lines ~278–290: `nextIdle` (Ctrl Space `a`) - lines ~378–430: tab-bar counts "N working" / "N idle · jump" - the prefix key handler (search for `"a"`) - lines ~530–545: the close `ConfirmDialog` text "… is still working (output Ns ago) …" - The tab dots: search for `tone` / `StatusGlyph` in the tab rendering. - `CommandPalette.tsx` (lines ~68–78): the terminal items, whose `secondary` includes `t.status` and whose badge is ``. - `ui/status.ts` (the `term` kind, lines ~29–36) and `ui/StatusBadge.tsx`: after this change nothing may use `kind="term"`. Remove the term mapping and update `ui/status.test.ts` and `ui/components.test.tsx` to match. If a later pane bar needs a tone for "exited with ≠ 0", use the `bad` tone directly. - `pages/Terminals.css`, `Shell.css`, `pages/Runs.css`: delete the CSS that only these elements used (`.tsb-chip`, `.tpane.idle`, the needs-you section styles, …). Check with grep that no class is left unused or missing. - Tests to update: - `pages/Terminals.test.tsx`: chips, NEEDS YOU, Ctrl Space a, the close confirmation - `Shell.test.tsx`: the status block counts and the Terminals badge - `pages/Runs.test.tsx`: the `card-idle` card - `pages/layout.test.ts`, if it touches filters - Run `grep -rn "idle\|working\|filter-\|NEEDS\|card-idle\|waiting on you\|next idle" apps/graph-manager/src/web` and resolve every hit. - Docs: - `apps/graph-manager/README.md`: - line ~70: the status block (now only runs live / runs failed) - line ~72: the Runs cards - line ~74: the Terminals sidebar - line ~87: the keyboard table row; drop "`a` jump to the next idle agent" - `TESTING.md`: - line ~142: the status block - line ~173: drop `?filter=working|idle|other` - lines ~174–175: the close confirmation now depends on the foreground process - line ~228: the checklist item - `docs/wiki/features/graph-manager-design.md`: replace the decision row "An idle terminal counts as "waiting on you"" with a row for GMD-15 ("Terminal statuses removed from the UI | The user doesn't want working/idle/other labels; the 3 s output heuristic was a guess anyway | GMD-15"). Also drop the "asked a question" follow-up. ## Step-by-step tasks 1. **Sidebar** (`TerminalSidebar.tsx`): - Remove `TermFilter`, `FILTERS`, `matchesFilter`, `workingFor`, `idleFor`, the chips and the "no match" text. - `groupTerminals(terminals, workspaces)` returns one section per workspace (label `OWNER/REPO`, upper-cased fullPath, with a count), ordered as the workspaces list, then `WORKSPACES ROOT`. There is no NEEDS YOU section. - Item sub-line: `t.process ?? "shell"`. No time, no tone, no status glyph. Use a neutral terminal icon or nothing in the glyph slot. - Keep the run chips and the pane-number badge, and keep `shortDuration`/`last4` if still used elsewhere. - Footer: only `Ctrl Space 1–4 focus pane` (add `Ctrl Space n new terminal` if it fits). 2. **Panes** (`TerminalPane.tsx`): no status badge in the header and no `.idle` class. The header is pane number, title, workspace, run chip, maximise, ×. Keep the exited bar exactly as is. 3. **Terminals.tsx:** - Remove the filter param, `onFilter`, the tab-bar counts, `nextIdle` and the `a` prefix key. - Tabs have no status dot. - Close confirmation: a new helper `isShell(name)`. Plain shells are `bash sh zsh fish dash ash tcsh csh ksh pwsh` (compare the basename, ignoring a leading `-`). - Ask only when the terminal has not exited and `process` is set and is not a shell. - Dialog: title `Close “”?`, body `<process> is running. Closing the tab ends it and its scrollback.`, cancel "Keep running", confirm "Close terminal" (danger). - Otherwise close right away. 4. **Shell.tsx:** - The status block has only the "runs live" and "runs failed" rows. - The Terminals nav badge is `<span className="nav-count">{terminals.length}</span>` when > 0. - No `termDot` on the rail. - Remove `working`/`idle` from the counts. 5. **Runs.tsx / Runs.css:** remove the "Terminals idle" card and the `terminals` read if unused. Make the cards grid 3 columns and keep it responsive. 6. **CommandPalette.tsx:** terminal items have the secondary `<workspace or cwd>` (plus ` · <process>` when known) and no badge. 7. **ui/status.ts / StatusBadge:** remove the `term` kind, then update `ui/status.test.ts` and `ui/components.test.tsx`. 8. **Tests:** update the tests above, and add these regressions: - `Terminals.test.tsx`: - the sidebar renders no chips and no "NEEDS YOU" for a mix of terminals with `status` working, idle and exited - the sub-line is the process name - closing a terminal whose `process` is `node` asks first; one whose `process` is `bash` closes without a dialog - Ctrl Space `a` does nothing - `Shell.test.tsx`: the status block has exactly 2 rows, and the Terminals badge shows the terminal count. - `Runs.test.tsx`: there is no `card-idle`. 9. **Docs:** README, TESTING.md and the wiki, as listed above. 10. **Look at it:** build and run graph-manager with the fake forge, open a few terminals (one running `node -e 'setInterval(()=>{},1000)'`, one `exit 0`), and take screenshots of `/terminals` (1 and 2×2 layouts), the nav and `/runs` in light and dark with `agent-browser`. Confirm that no "working", "idle", "other" or "waiting on you" text appears anywhere: `agent-browser eval 'document.body.innerText.match(/working|idle|waiting on you|NEEDS YOU/gi)'` → `null` on each page. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] No page shows "working", "idle", "other" chips, "NEEDS YOU" or "waiting on you". The `innerText` check above gives `null` on `/runs`, `/terminals`, `/workspaces` and `/settings`. - [ ] Sidebar items show the title, the process name, run chips and pane numbers. Sections are per workspace, then WORKSPACES ROOT. - [ ] The nav status block has 2 rows (runs live, runs failed). The Terminals badge is the terminal count. - [ ] Runs has 3 cards. - [ ] Closing a terminal running `node` asks first; closing a terminal at its `bash` prompt does not. - [ ] `exit 1` still shows "Process exited with code 1" with Restart and Close. - [ ] `git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution` is empty. - [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass. ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test -w graph-manager grep -rn "NEEDS YOU\|waiting on you\|next idle\|card-idle" apps/graph-manager/src/web # nothing git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution # empty npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager # then agent-browser as in step 10 (see the graph-manager section of TESTING.md for the start commands; fake forge tokens gh-good / gl-good) ``` The environment may have `NODE_ENV=production`. If `npm ci` skips devDependencies, use `NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev`. Known environment failure: `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` "exits 2 at startup when --provider claude is not on the PATH" fails wherever a real `claude` is installed next to `node`. Ignore that one case only.
